rationale:
loancash.co.uk was the LAST of the five register-less finance sites named in RFC_060 section 1d; the other four (lendzy 695, loanzy 697, farmerinsurance 698+713, loancalculator 699) are done. It had ZERO evidence_base rows [MEASURED 2026-09-03] - an ABSENT register, not an empty one - beside 14 other current specs, on a deployed site serving 30 pages. The owner directed this lane to populate it on 2026-09-03. RFC_060 section 4: populating these registers is content work, needs no RFC, and is the single highest-value action arising from that RFC.

This site is the highest-risk of the five and the reason is structural, not rhetorical: the other four calculate or compare, whereas loancash EXPLAINS THE RULES THEMSELVES to people in financial difficulty. Its 30 served pages carry 338 regulatory-shaped sentences [MEASURED 2026-09-03, crawled at the artefact with an invented-URL 404 control], of which only THREE cite a rule number. The rest state hard figures - 0.8%, £15, 100%, 8 weeks, 6 months, 60 days, 3% per month - in plain English with no citation and nothing re-checking them.

This also discharges a request already on file. The loancash_couk_fca_validation lane wrote on 2026-08-11, after verifying the three price-cap constants by hand: 'What is still true is the second half of the worry: nothing is checking ... What actually earns its keep is something that reads the rulebook and shouts if it disagrees with what is on our page.' That is this mechanism. That lane also named the complaint-deadline calculator as its highest-value unchecked item, because limitation periods - unlike the price cap, static since 02/01/2015 - do move. Three of the nineteen facts register exactly those deadlines.

Three facts carry corrects_site_citation. The served copy is NOT touched: rewriting published prose on an automated finding is authority the owner withheld (bugs_open/320 section 15, the 695 precedent).

plan.summary: One additive migration creating loancash.co.uk's evidence_base register: 19 facts (11 FCA Handbook rules, 8 statutory) and the 6-pattern sibling lending banned-claims set. Guard aborts if any evidence_base row exists; DO/RAISE verify asserts 19 facts, 19 with a handbook/legislation URL and a substantive quote, 19 naming a CONC/DISP/statutory rule, exactly 3 with corrects_site_citation, and 6 banned_claims. Plus a ROLLBACK file whose guard refuses once the daily refresher has superseded the row. No code changes; no served copy changed.
plan.risks:
(1) A quote that does not survive the refresher's extraction classifies as citation_lost - drift - every day for ever, a false alarm indistinguishable from a real one. Mitigated by verifying all 19 through the PRODUCTION functions (cmd/fcaquotecheck -> datahelpers.VisibleTextFromHTML / QuoteFoundInText) with a deliberately-absent control returning false in every run, not by inspection. This caught a real defect in this very submission: the DISP 2.8.2(2)(b) quote was first transcribed with commas where the source has parentheses and returned FALSE; it was corrected and re-verified true.
(2) handbook.fca.org.uk returns HTTP 200 for EVERY path including invented rules (documented LANDMINE), so status is worthless as an existence test. All URLs confirmed by <title>, and the URL STORED is the one that answered after the redirect. legislation.gov.uk gets the same discipline.
(3) BANNED-CLAIM WIDTH, the risk that would not have been visible in a coverage count: the 'shared finance set' exists in TWO widths. lendzy.co.uk carries a bare \bno credit checks?\b; loanzy/loancalculator carry a narrow variant requiring the product noun. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] the BARE variant fires on this site's CORRECT consumer advice that an employer salary advance involves 'no interest and no credit check' (1 hit); the narrow variant fires 0 times across all 30 pages. The narrow variant is adopted, deliberately. All 6 patterns were compiled with the production prefix regexp.Compile("(?i)"+p) (claims.go:468) and each fired against a positive control: 6/6 compile, 6/6 match their positive, 0/6 match anything served.
(4) STRUCTURAL LIMIT, stated not hidden: neither host has a rule-level URL, so the refresher keeps QUOTES honest but not the `rule` field. Until RFC_060 section 3d/Q6's rule-span checker ships, `rule` is human-verified - checked by hand against each provision's own heading on 2026-09-03.
(5) Arming the register arms ScanUnregisteredNumbers on this site. Not measured against loancash's components in this round; the regulatory-citation exclusions (fad209b92) are live fleet-wide, and the site's numerals are overwhelmingly the very figures now registered.

edits.rationale: The register. DO/RAISE guard refusing to run if any evidence_base row exists for the site; one INSERT of the 19-fact + 6-pattern JSON; DO/RAISE verify asserting all five properties. Verification is DO/RAISE throughout because a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT. BOTH guards were mutation-tested against the live database on 2026-09-03: changing the expected fact count 19->18 aborted with '738 VERIFY: expected 19 facts, found 19'; changing the guard predicate aborted before the INSERT. The whole migration was then run against the live database with COMMIT swapped for ROLLBACK - guard passed, INSERT 0 1, verify NOTICE fired, nothing left behind (loancash still has 0 evidence_base rows and 14 current specs).

Removes exactly the row 738 created, and REFUSES if it is no longer the current one. This is not defensive boilerplate: RUNBOOK_lendzy section 8d records that the rollback guard EXPIRES at the first refresher pass by design - the daily sweep supersedes the row with one created_by 'evidence-refresher'. After that the row is no longer purely 738's to remove and a human should look, so the guard aborts rather than guesses. The file says so.

grounded_in: RFC_060 section 4: 'populating registers for the five register-less finance sites ... belongs to the site lanes, needs no RFC, and would deliver most of the benefit of (ii) without any code at all. If only one thing happens as a result of this RFC, it should be that.'
RFC_060 section 1d re-measured 2026-09-03: four of the five are done; loancash.co.uk is the last, 'still none - no session assigned; owner informed'.
[MEASURED 2026-09-03] SELECT count(*) FROM site_specs WHERE site_id='ee4a8199-4f5b-4e2e-88ce-01e600721b74' AND aspect='evidence_base' returns 0, against 14 current specs and 30 pages.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03] All 30 served pages crawled; invented-URL control returns 404 (so this is not a parked domain answering everything); 338 regulatory-shaped sentences extracted, 3 carrying a rule id.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03] cmd/fcaquotecheck, production matcher: CONC 5A.2 four quotes true / control false (visible=11259); CONC 6.7 true/false; CONC 7.6 two true / control false; CONC 5.2A true/false; DISP 1.6 true/false; DISP 2.8 three true / control false; SI 2020/1311 regs 16/24/26/32 each true/false; SI 2013/2589 true/false; FSMA s.19 and s.23 each true/false. 19/19 true, control false in every run.

CONC 5A.2.14R verbatim: charges connected with a breach must not, 'whether in relation to one breach or cumulatively in relation to multiple breaches of the agreement', exceed £15. The site's served copy: 'that fee is capped at £15 and can only be charged once per missed payment'.

CONC 7.6.12R verbatim: a firm must not make a further request if it has done so 'on two previous occasions and those previous payment requests have been refused'. The string '£1' appears NOWHERE in CONC 7.6 (searched the extracted visible text). The site's served copy: 'cannot take more than one payment attempt of over £1'. Its own CPA page says correctly: 'A lender can attempt to collect a payment using your CPA twice.'

CONC 5A is titled 'Prohibition from entering into agreements for high-cost short-term credit' and contains no affordability rule; CONC 5.2A.4R is 'A firm must undertake a reasonable assessment of the creditworthiness of a customer before'. The site's served copy: 'the affordability checks set out under CONC 5A'.

All 6 adopted patterns compile under regexp.Compile("(?i)"+p) and match their positive controls.
